## The delivery lifecycle {#delivery-lifecycle}

Between deliveries the landing page advertises no upcoming delivery. Scheduling a delivery takes the four steps below, and resetting after one takes two.

**Scheduling.**

- [ ] Fill the `delivery:` block in `_variables.yml` (date, venue/platform, event, mode, registration URL) and set `active: 'true'`. Re-render and push, and the landing page shows a "Next delivery" callout. Set `active: 'false'` again afterwards.
- [ ] Decide the extended-universe option at **T-2 weeks** against the go/no-go checklist in `_planning/extended-universe-spec.md`. If GO, the opt-in text there goes into the joining email.
- [ ] Decide recording. If recording: talk segments only, announced at the start of each recorded stretch, paused for hands-on and chat-heavy segments. Nothing in the day depends on the recording either way.
- [ ] Optionally create the prereg mirror form from `_planning/prereg-form-spec.md` and paste its URL into `_variables.yml`. The rendered declaration block is the primary record and the form only a backup, so skipping the form loses nothing.

**Resetting, before the next one.**

- [ ] Export the responses Sheet (File → Download → CSV) and commit it as a date-stamped snapshot (e.g. `data/class_results_2026-06-16.csv`); refresh `data/class_results.csv` per `facilitator/live-results-setup.md` if you want the archived cohort visible on the evergreen site.
- [ ] Clear (or archive to a second tab) the old rows in the live Sheet so that the chart opens almost empty for the next cohort. **Do not touch the Form, the Worker, or the field schema.** The pipeline works, and only the rows change from one cohort to the next.

---

## The week before

- [ ] Click once through the tab switching for Parts 3–4 (deck → the spec-menu page → the results page and back), so that the order is familiar on the day. It is the one sequence that you run live several times during the day.
- [ ] Send joining instructions: setup page link, the two-window/two-device tip, the optional pre-reading (listed on the setup page), and – if GO – the extended-universe opt-in text.
- [ ] Confirm the Multi100 slide in the deck against the registered protocol at osf.io/7snkz (the note on that slide asks for the actual wording of the registration, not a paraphrase).

## The night before

- [ ] Render the full site: `quarto render` from the workspace root; check no errors; push; if the site is published, confirm the Pages build completes on GitHub Actions.
- [ ] **Live results loop** (full setup + checks in `facilitator/live-results-setup.md`): submit one anonymous test row via the Form (incognito), confirm it reaches the Sheet, confirm the Worker returns the sheet as CSV, press *Run Code* on the live [Multiverse]({{< var live-results-url >}}) page and see the test dot. Then delete the test row.
- [ ] **Prereg block loop**: open the workspace zip fresh (download it as a participant would), complete the declaration block with a dummy spec, render, and check the rendered block and timestamp. If the mirror form exists, submit one dummy row and delete it.
- [ ] **Browser lab cold load**: open the live page of `exercise/browser-lab.qmd` in a private window on the venue-typical connection; time the webR engine load; run the first chunk and the Task 3 reproduce chunk (t = −3.804).
- [ ] Confirm both OSF nodes load logged-out: osf.io/6zqct (fork) and osf.io/8rtwe (archive); confirm osf.io/h7432 shows the replication component (the scavenger target).
- [ ] Prepare the catch-up card, the help doc, and the day-plan message (texts below) as ready-to-paste snippets.
- [ ] Charge everything; second device signed in to Teams as a participant-view check.

## Opening the room {#opening-the-virtual-room--30-minutes-before}

- [ ] Open the Teams meeting early; enable chat for everyone; check breakout rooms are available (they are optional – nothing depends on them).
- [ ] Seed the chat: site URL · browser-lab URL · cheatsheet URL · the timestamped day plan (the standing order if the host drops: "follow the day plan; finish the current task or take the break early; I will rejoin").
- [ ] Post the interaction key: "green circle emoji = working · STUCK = I need help · answers to quizzes: type but hold until I say go".
- [ ] Share the deck; keep three tabs ready to switch: the deck, the spec menu, the Multiverse page.
- [ ] If recording: announce it now and state what is and is not recorded.

## Run sheet

Times in the part tables are part-relative: 0:00 is the start of that part. The clock below maps them onto the next delivery.

| Segment | Romanian time (EEST) | UK time (BST) |
|---|---|---|
| Part 1 – Credibility and tools | 10:00–11:30 | 08:00–09:30 |
| Break | 11:30–12:00 | 09:30–10:00 |
| Part 2 – The claim and its estimand | 12:00–13:30 | 10:00–11:30 |
| Lunch | 13:30–14:30 | 11:30–12:30 |
| Part 3 – Reproduction and exploration | 14:30–16:00 | 12:30–14:00 |
| Break | 16:00–16:30 | 14:00–14:30 |
| Part 4 – Multiverse and preregistration | 16:30–18:00 | 14:30–16:00 |

You are two hours behind the class all day, so its 10:00 start is your 08:00. Everything you post in chat should give Romanian times, because those are the times that the summer school published.

**Three stretches of the deck are optional depth**, marked on screen and skippable in one keystroke: the R tutorial (Part 2, 10 slides), the methodological tutorial (Part 3, 12 slides) and the multiverse tutorial (Part 4, 8 slides). Five slides in the tools segment of Part 1 have the same mark. Decide on the day how much of each the class wants. The timings below assume you walk roughly half of each; walking all three in full costs about 25 minutes you do not have, and skipping all three entirely leaves the hands-on tasks with more room than they need.

### Driving 148 slides {#deck-navigation}

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| space · right arrow · clicker | next slide. **Always exactly one slide** – the deck is set to linear mode so that no clicker press can skip a segment |
| **`d`** | switch between the **extended** and the **lean** deck, live. In lean mode the optional slides are taken out of the deck: every key skips them and the count drops from 148 to 113 |
| **`]`** and **`[`** | jump to the **next / previous part** |
| **`g`** | **jump bar**: type a few letters of any slide title, press Enter |
| **`s`** | speaker view (notes, timer, next slide) |
| **`f`** · **`esc`** | fullscreen · slide overview |

**The readout, top right,** has two lines. The first names the part and gives both positions (`PART 3 · 8/24 · 90/148`). The second is a badge that is always present and shows the state of the deck:

| Badge | Means |
|---|---|
| green **extended** | the full deck, and this slide is part of the main flow |
| burgundy **optional** | the full deck, and this slide belongs to an optional run. The figure beside it is your position inside that run – `3/12` |
| amber **lean** | the optional runs are switched off |
| a burgundy **dot** before the amber badge | lean mode, and an optional run has been lifted out right here – either the slide you are on is the last before it, or the first after it. Press `d` if the class wants it |

The readout is hidden on the title slide, the part dividers and the break slides, where it would otherwise overlap the dark background beside the brand mark.

**Opening the lean deck directly.** Add `?depth=0` to the address and the optional runs are gone before the first slide appears – useful if you already know the class. Without it the deck opens complete. If you follow a link to a slide that is hidden in lean mode, you land on the first slide after the hidden run.

**The escape hatch on screen.** The first slide of each optional run has a small grey link at the top right, which says how many slides the run contains and where the main flow resumes. Clicking it jumps straight there, so it does with the mouse for one run what `d` does for all of them.

## Online and in-person cue sheet {#online--in-person-cue-sheet}

The materials are identical online and in person. What changes is how people answer, flag trouble and pair up, and the table below lists what to swap.

| Beat | Online (Teams) | In person |
|---|---|---|
| Quiz / waterfall answers | type in chat, hold until "go" | write on paper, hands up on "go" (or Vevox if the venue has it) |
| Working / stuck status | green-circle emoji / "STUCK" in chat | green / red-orange sticky notes |
| Roll-call | Teams "raise hand" | visual sweep |
| Pair moments | breakout rooms if available; scripted chat variant otherwise | table pairs |
| Rescues | buddy-chunk on the shared screen | facilitator circulates |
| The live chart | everyone opens the Multiverse page themselves | projector + own laptops |
| Form links | pasted in chat | QR codes on the slides |
| Breaks | countdown slide + "back at :xx" in chat | countdown slide + verbal |
| Facilitator absent | published day plan = standing order | n/a |

## Chat protocols and ready-to-paste texts {#chat-protocols-and-ready-to-paste-texts}

**Waterfall:** "Type your answer now but DON'T send – hold it. … Go." Holding the answers back keeps each one independent of the others, and releasing them together is what produces the wall-of-identical-values beats.

**Help:** a STUCK in chat is the first flag. The standing **help doc**, a shared editable document whose link goes into the chat at the start, is the second place to look and the place where errors get pasted. Check it at the minutes that the run sheet names, not continuously. Rescues run in the main room by buddy-chunk: their spec, my webR or IDE, and everyone watching learns from it.

**Silent class:** wait 20 seconds, then take reactions (thumbs) as the minimal response, and name one or two people gently ("Sam, what did you get?"). Two substantive answers from twenty participants are enough to proceed.

**Catch-up card (paste at Part 3 re-entry):**

> Just back? You missed nothing you can't recover: (1) if Task 2 (the estimand and the DAG) is unfinished, run its DAG chunk as-is and come back to the wording later; (2) Task 3 is the reproduction – the target is t = −3.804 and there is a full solution on the page; (3) Task 4 is exploration, so just try two specifications and submit one. Flag STUCK and I'll come to you in the run window.

**Facilitator-drop standing order (seeded in chat at open):**

> If I drop off the call: keep going. The day plan (link) has the timings – finish the current task or take the break early. I will rejoin as soon as I can.

---

## The cutting order {#compression-ladders-with-trigger-times}

When time runs short, cut from the optional-depth runs before anything else, so that the time comes out of a tutorial before it comes out of a task.

- **Part 1** – trigger 0:30: cut the Miske moderators slide to one line and compress the open-research practices table to one sentence per row. Trigger 1:05: drop the two per-tool optional-depth slides (languages, editors) and the licences slide; keep plain-text-survives and what-the-tools-cannot-do.
- **Part 2** – trigger 0:50 (running long after estimands): the DAG crash course drops the selection-and-feedback slide to one sentence and reaches the half-built graph sooner. Trigger 1:12: skip the R tutorial entirely and go straight into Task 2. Trigger 1:22: Task 2 to demo-only – run it on my screen, they note the output and finish over lunch. The estimand waterfall is never compressed.
- **Part 3** – trigger 0:57: the methodological tutorial drops to its three core slides (outcome, claim alignment, estimators). Trigger 1:10: Task 4 shortens to two `try_spec()` calls and a submission – but everybody still submits, because Part 4 opens on those dots.
- **Part 4** – trigger 0:33: skip the multiverse tutorial, keep 'what the curve leaves out'. Trigger 0:55: drop the scavenger beat and shorten the inference module, leaving the detail to the reading. The class-chart debrief, the fork-importance reveal and the preregistration moment are never compressed.

**Never cut:** the five-analyst reveal and its software column · the estimand waterfall · the half-built DAG and its adjustment set · the reproduction waterfall · the Task 4 submission · the preregistration moment · the fork-importance reveal.

## Contingencies {#contingency-table}

Each row names the first move, not the only one, and every ladder ends at a point from which the session can carry on.

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| **A participant's webR fails mid-task** | The cheatsheet ladder: hard reload + rerun chunks above → second browser → buddy-chunk on my screen → grid lookup + hand submission (any spec looks up in its shard under `data/grid/`, as the cheatsheet sets out). Everyone still submits a dot. |
| **A participant's installation breaks** | Switch them to the browser lab, which holds the whole exercise; their workspace survives for later. |
| **The live chart fails during the day** (Form, Worker, CORS) | Rung 1: `results.qmd` falls back to the committed `data/class_results.csv` automatically. Rung 2: pull the Sheet CSV, commit, re-render locally, share my screen. Rung 3: the static 840-spec curve and the five-analyst slides are enough for the debrief. Submissions are safe in the Sheet whatever happens to the chart, because nothing upstream depends on it. |
| **Breakout rooms unavailable** | Every pair moment has a scripted chat variant. |
| **OSF slow/unreachable during the scavenger** | Show h7432 on my screen and the beat still works. The data never depend on OSF being reachable, because they ship with the workspace and the browser lab. |
| **My connection drops** | The standing order in chat: participants continue the current task or break early; I rejoin. The pipeline keeps collecting – it is entirely independent of the call. |
| **A participant cannot speak/hear** | Everything essential is chat-and-screen; deliver any spoken instruction in chat on request. |
| **Recording objections** | Recording is optional, so stop it; nothing depends on it. |
| **Prereg mirror form fails** | The rendered block is the record; carry on. |

## Expected numbers {#answer-keys-and-expected-numbers}

- Warm-up matrix question set: 1 = reproducibility (a failed attempt is still reproducibility) · 2 = the grey area between reproducibility and robustness – argue both ways · 3 = replicability · 4 = generalisability.
- Task 3 (the same in the workspace and the browser lab): b = −0.00347, SE = 0.00091, **t = −3.804**, df = 233, N = 270 (`EUframes_cy.csv`) – the value on record for C6HJR, reproduced directly from `euframes`.
- The data-preparation material is off the running order and out of the deck. If you want to raise it on the day, the facts, the withdrawn slides and their speaker notes are in `_planning/block2-error-story-withdrawn-2026-07-30.md`, local to your machine – paste any block straight back into the deck.
- Family axis (a first-class menu axis; not part of the Multi100 Task-2 menu, which fixed unemployment and, implicitly, the gaussian scale): beta submissions report **z**, not t. In the browser lab every spec, beta included, is read from the pre-computed grid, so `report_result()` takes no fit; the workspace fits beta live. Grid-lookup fallback: any spec looks up in its shard under `data/grid/` – the file is named by the six Level 1 choices other than the scoring rule, and the row by the other eight, the scoring rule among them; the cheatsheet has the recipe. The beta family is pre-computed at the standard measurement settings only. Beta twin of C6HJR's published Multi100 specification: b(logit) = −0.01399, **z = −4.075**, r = −0.258 (C6HJR's Gaussian r = −0.242: same direction, still significant, slightly stronger).
- Claim-alignment (the class convention, set on the spec menu): negative framings (`mcomm`, `mlib`, `mneg`) reverse-coded 1 − y before fitting; sign of b, t and r flips, magnitudes and p untouched (exactly so for beta too). Aligned r runs **−0.70 to +0.24** (gaussian; beta reaches +0.29) – so a class dot above ≈ +0.25 is almost certainly an **un-recoded negative framing**, not a genuine contrary result; name that in the debrief. One caveat from the growth-predictor axis: legitimately aligned growth-predictor dots can reach ≈ +0.37 – check the declared spec before calling it.
- Analyst placement (share of grid more negative, claim-aligned): KEVF1 15.8% · KQXUE 21.5% · C6HJR 49.6% · 018OL 63.1% · PRL47 67.9%. The two person-level analysts (KEVF1, PRL47) sit at the extremes; the constrained baseline falls almost exactly at the median of the aligned grid.
- Task-1 layer (slide after analyst placement): free phase = five different questions – 018OL GDP p.c. level, KEVF1 growth, PRL47 a GDP battery; only KQXUE and C6HJR used unemployment – with one shared recorded verdict ('evidence for the claim'). No standardised Task-1 effect sizes exist in the public Multi100 data (verdict + free text only). My own Task 1 (`mposframe ~ growth + unemp`, two-way FE, World Bank series) reproduces from the committed as-submitted panel: unemployment t = −4.72, growth ns – standardisation *weakened* my result.
- Predictor axis (a first-class menu axis; menu + lab lookup in the `data/grid/` shards; at the standard measurement settings the growth half is 840 cells across both families; not part of the Multi100 Task-2 menu, though Task 1 shows three of five analysts freely chose GDP measures in place of unemployment): GDP growth as claim carrier, raw form only – affine forms are t-inert (centred≡raw, log-z≡log), which is why the deduplicated grid holds 840 distinct analyses. Growth predictor (840 rows in the full grid): 70.5% claim-direction / 46.9% significant, aligned max +0.37 – direction without significance, matching KQXUE's Task-1 growth null. Growth mirror of my Task-1 model on the EU-frames panel: b = +0.00167, t = 1.59, ns. Growth polarity: claim-aligned reporting flips the sign (lab lookup does it).
- Fork importance: outcome 49.7% · residual/interactions 49.2% · sample 0.7 · estimator 0.4 · predictor form/copredictor/weights ≈ 0.
- Sign flips (mcosmo universe, 140 specs): 41 wrong-sign; 33 in `pooled_cl`, 8 in `fe_twoway`; 24 of the 41 in bailout-excluding samples (halved from the pre-dedupe counts – every distinct analysis appeared exactly twice before, so shares are invariant).
- Constrained universe: 140 specs · 70.7% negative · 57.1% negative-and-significant. Discussion-beat target: "no verdict without a null for dependent specifications – that is what a curve-level permutation test would supply (the design in the inference reading)."
- Baseline percentile (for participants without their own submission): −3.804 ⇒ ≈ 49.6% on the claim-aligned scale.

## Debrief questions {#debrief-question-bank}

Choose by what the class chart actually shows, not by the order below.

1. **Sign flip:** "Did anyone's specification flip the sign? If not – after seeing the flips chart, where would you have had to stand in the menu to flip it?"
2. **Significance loss:** "Did any spec lose significance? Reason to doubt the claim, or to scrutinise that spec?"
3. **Axis that moved most:** "Before I showed the decomposition – which axis did you bet on, and why did most of us get it wrong?"
4. **Justification quality:** "Whose DAG settled their choice? Whose DAG could have justified three different specs equally well?"
5. **Preregistration felt:** "Did completing the block before running change how the result felt when it landed? Would you have chosen differently after seeing it?"
6. **Robustness tolerance:** "Multi100 used ±0.05 and ±0.20 d. Is the claim robust by the tight standard here? The loose one? Who gets to choose the tolerance for a policy claim?"
7. **Against the five analysts:** "The class overlaps the five analysts' range. Is that reassuring or circular? What would a result *outside* their range have meant?"
8. **Percentile literacy:** "Your percentile places you among 840 defensible alternatives. What does a 10th-percentile analyst owe their reader that a 50th-percentile analyst does not?"
9. **The three Rs on one paper:** "This paper failed reproduction, survived robustness in sign but not magnitude, and sign-flipped in replication. Which R should worry us most – and does it depend on what the finding is used for?"
10. **The inference gap:** "If a curve-level permutation test came back at p = .30, what would survive of today? What if it came back at p = .004?"

- [ ] Run the reset procedure from the top of this guide: export + commit the date-stamped snapshot, rotate the Sheet rows.
- [ ] Export the feedback form responses.
- [ ] Improvement log – record: which segment ran longest; did the estimand idea land (could people write one, did the waterfall show real spread); did the extra time in Part 2 give the DAG segment the space it needed, or expose thin material; how many declarations before the proceed rule fired; did every participant submit a dot (which ladder rungs fired); did webR hold on home connections; Teams frictions (chat scale, breakouts, share switching).
